jobs.desc: Backend at a fully digital insurtech. Building and evolving the insurance core and the services behind the full policy lifecycle: Java + Spring Boot microservices with PostgreSQL on Kubernetes. TDD, code review and AI-assisted development with Claude. Observability with Grafana, OpenTelemetry and Sentry.

Worked at the intersection of software engineering and AI. Built the knowledge layer that lets AI understand a team's architecture and conventions — agent design, prompt engineering, context management.
Backend microservice features for job integration flows, with unit tests on every feature delivered. Cloud migration, technical debt reduction, monitoring with Grafana and Datadog on Kubernetes.
Backend microservices with Java 8–17 and Spring Boot, plus frontend features in Angular. Flyway migrations on PostgreSQL and Oracle. Agile delivery with CI/CD. Internal Women in Tech bootcamp.

about.p1: I started with <mark class="y">words and human languages</mark> and ended up migrating to <mark class="c">code and programming languages</mark>. The path wasn’t easy: after studying English Philology I spent six years in logistics, and in 2022, at 30, I broke with my “previous life” and dove into a Java bootcamp. I loved it and wanted more, so while working I also took the higher vocational degree in Multiplatform Application Development.
about.p2: And now, with AI, natural language turns out to be a way of programming again: a good part of the job is explaining precisely what you want, giving an agent the right context and reviewing what it returns with a critical eye. That’s where <mark class="v">the philologist and the dev help each other out</mark>.
about.p3: I currently work as a <mark class="p">Backend Developer</mark> at Tuio, a fully digital insurtech, on the insurance core with Java and Spring Boot. I started as a Java/Angular fullstack developer, moved towards backend, and spent a while designing agents and context so AI could understand how a team works.
about.p4: I know what it’s like to start from scratch and feel lost, and it has made me more patient with others and with myself. Outside work I build small projects to learn, sing in the Diatessaron Choir and write on Medium when I have something to say.
